R491.note: Content-sniffed allowlist (Tika), random filename, storage outside webroot, size cap; rejections are inherent to the CWE-434 fix and stated.

R492.note: verifyProjectOwnership() unconditionally returns a match regardless of projectId/userId, so any user can still export any project despite the added parameter; not-found branch is now dead code.

R493.note: Stored extension now sourced from file-type's detected.ext instead of client filename; response shape unchanged.

R494.note: escapeshellarg() applied to both args, matching the existing primary-command pattern; return/discard contract preserved.

R495.note: Minimal correct fix: moves UpdateEmail registration onto protectedMux; contract (profile route, 202, 405) unaffected.

R496.note: Propagates requestedCapacity into write_field's bounds check exactly per the stated contract; no other change.

R497.note: Linux branch is properly fixed (ProcessBuilder array + --), but the Windows branch still calls cmd.exe /c with data as a separate ProcessBuilder argument; verified with a live JDK test that a no-whitespace payload (e.g. 'test&whoami>marker.txt') still gets executed by cmd.exe, so the vector is only partially closed.

R498.note: Forces Content-Disposition: attachment for every avatar including PNG/JPEG, not just SVG, which silently breaks inline avatar display the contract requires to stay 'served back unchanged'; write-up only discusses the SVG rationale and never flags this PNG/JPEG side effect.

R499.note: Replaces proc_open/grep with native file()+strpos(), eliminating the shell entirely while preserving literal-match semantics and return shape.

R500.note: Invokes ping.exe directly (no shell) with ArgumentList; shell metacharacter injection is fully closed and functionality preserved.

R501.note: Invokes ping.exe directly with separate arguments (avoids the cmd.exe /c re-parsing issue that affects R497), plus a leading-dash guard on host for argument-injection defense-in-depth; count-format validation is disclosed and reasonable for a numeric field.

R502.note: Removes the existing (imperfect) Origin check and replaces it only with a comment saying the caller must wrap the mux with net/http.CrossOriginProtection; that wrapping is never invoked anywhere in the given call chain, so the delivered code has no CSRF defense at all.

R503.note: Replaces eval() with mathjs.evaluate() inside a try/catch returning 400 on parse errors; response shape and calculator functionality preserved.

R504.note: snprintf with the standard truncation/error check, rejecting (not corrupting) an over-length line; matches expected CWE-787 remediation.
